scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03).
59% (1785/3025) of disputed bills in Aug-Sep 2026 were built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED (E-02).
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) (E-05).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03). The majority (59%, E-02) of disputed bills were built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates, and no tariff change occurred (E-04), so the surge is driven primarily by a billing-side defect in processing/validating accepted actual reads downstream of read collection - not by field-read/estimation shortfalls, which affect only a minority (41%, E-02) of disputes despite a real route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01) - and not by slow dispute response, which remains within SLA (E-05).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: E-01 still shows manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a real field-collection shortfall. It no longer supports that this shortfall drives the 1240 ESTIMATED-dispute population's estimate-substitution, since E-12 shows that population is almost entirely AMI-channel accounts rejected on billing import (1184/1240), not manual-read accounts failing field collection.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-AI-AUTOFIX-FRAMING.statement: Dispute tickets are driven by identifiable billing errors that an AI agent can both diagnose and automatically correct, resolving the surge.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: A degradation in AMI meter-read delivery or validation (ORG-AMI/MDMS) since August is producing missing or bad interval reads that lead to estimated or incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Contracted manual meter-reading (MeterWorks) has had degraded route completion or delayed uploads since August, increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August introduced a defect in read acceptance or estimate-substitution logic, causing incorrect bills.

H-TICKET-INTAKE-SHIFT.statement: The apparent dispute surge partly reflects a change in CS ticket logging, categorization, or SLA tracking rather than an actual increase in incorrect bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-CALC-ERROR.statement: A billing calculation or tariff-application defect affecting bills built from ACTUAL meter reads (not a read-collection or estimation failure) accounts for the majority of disputed bills.

H-RESPONSE-TIME-ADEQUATE.statement: Dispute response times already meet SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA across 2440 tickets), so the surge problem is ticket volume/bill correctness, not response speed.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged above a high-consumption threshold, forcing fallback to estimate substitution and generating disputes, as seen in 1184/1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills.

H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares a raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling applied, which may systematically misclassify legitimate consumption as high if register units are not already in m3, driving the mass AMI-read rejections seen in E-12.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-completion log shows manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a real shortfall in field meter-read collection during the dispute-surge window.

E-01 still shows manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a real field-collection shortfall. It no longer supports that this shortfall drives the 1240 ESTIMATED-dispute population's estimate-substitution, since E-12 shows that population is almost entirely AMI-channel accounts rejected on billing import (1184/1240), not manual-read accounts failing field collection.

Disputed bills split by read type show 1785 (59%) are ACTUAL reads versus 1240 (41%) ESTIMATED, so most disputes are not simply estimate-substitution bills from missing reads. This points toward a billing-side calculation/tariff issue affecting bills built from accepted actual reads, not just a read-collection/estimation gap.

E-02 still shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED (41%) vs 1785 ACTUAL (59%). It no longer supports that the ESTIMATED subset reflects a manual-read/field-collection estimation gap, since E-12 shows that same 1240-bill population is almost entirely AMI-channel reads rejected on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not missing manual reads.

Monthly dispute-ticket counts (E-03) show roughly 600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) jumping to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a real doubling of ticket volume coincident with the reported surge window. The data only quantifies the magnitude/timing of the symptom; it says nothing about which upstream cause (field reads, AMI, billing rules, calculation errors, or ticket-intake process changes) produced it.

E-04 shows the billing-db tariff change log returned 0 records, meaning no tariff rate/structure change was logged in the queried period; a changed tariff definition therefore cannot explain the billing errors behind the dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times (E-05) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning response times are currently within SLA for the vast majority of tickets. This indicates the dispute surge is not driven by slow ticket handling/response speed, which was the implicit framing behind the "auto-answer" request.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which echoes the already-confirmed tool finding E-04 that the tariff change log has zero records for the period. As a stakeholder claim it is non-authoritative and adds no new decision-relevant information beyond what E-04 already established.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) attributes the field route completion shortfall (E-01: 0.88 vs 0.95) to being three readers short since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for affected customers. This is a non-authoritative claim from a stakeholder whose stated bias is to attribute problems to staffing and whose incentive is contract headcount increase; it also introduces a timing note (shortage since July) that precedes the August dispute surge onset, which the claim does not reconcile.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document confirms a contractual authorization structure: the utility can request field route priority changes, but execution requires runtime confirmation from the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), consistent with the existing K-DISPATCH constraint. It speaks to protected-action authorization/governance, not to the root cause of the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: This billing-db query returns 320 accounts billed with ESTIMATED reads in the last cycle across 40 distinct routes, giving account/route-level granularity but no linkage to dispute status, read-type dispute split, or the Aug-Sep two-month window used elsewhere (E-01/E-02). The count is markedly smaller than the ~1104 route-incomplete accounts implied by E-01's 0.88 completion rate, which is a weak signal that field-route shortfalls may not fully translate into estimated-billing volume, though period alignment ('last cycle' vs Aug-Sep) is unclear.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes returns 14 routes with below-target completion values (sample: R-00 at 0.70), adding route-level granularity to the manual-read completion shortfall already quantified in aggregate by E-01. The record has no time-period or dispute-linkage fields, so it cannot establish whether this shortfall overlaps temporally with the August dispute-surge onset (U-FIELD-TIMING) or confirm the A-OVERLAP assumption.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which if true would unblock the previously access-pending mdms-export query needed to test H-AMI-READ-FAILURE and address VOB-U-MDMS-ACCESS. It does not itself establish AMI read data content or confirm the claim, since mdms-export tool_health is still recorded as DEGRADED and this is an unverified stakeholder statement, not a tool/document record.

Of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (matching E-02's ESTIMATED count exactly), AMI-channel read events show 1184 (95%) had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on billing import, while only 56 (5%) genuinely had no AMI read received. This means the ESTIMATED-dispute population is almost entirely AMI-metered accounts whose valid reads were rejected by a billing import validation rule, not manual-read accounts failing field collection, and not AMI reads failing to arrive at all.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-13 shows billing-config logged a validation rule change, BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling=none), deployed 2026-08-01 — exactly at the dispute-surge onset (E-03). This is the first direct evidence of a billing-import rule change coincident with the surge, and its raw-register-vs-m3 comparison with no stated unit scaling is a plausible mechanism for the AMI-read rejections seen in E-12 (1184/1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION). BV-09 (label text, deployed 2026-03-02) is unrelated to the surge window.

E-14 shows firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3, while firmware v3.x meters report in plain m3. This unit mismatch, combined with BV-17's unscaled raw-register-vs-12-month-m3-history comparison (E-13), gives a concrete mechanism for why v4.2 meters' legitimate reads would appear inflated and be rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, consistent with E-12's finding that 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-dispute bills trace to firmware v4.2 AMI reads rejected on import.

U-LOCUS.question: Which specific step downstream of read collection - billing import validation rule change, bill calculation defect, or AMI read delivery/validation degradation - is the dominant cause of incorrect ACTUAL-read bills?
U-LOCUS.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation targets billing import rules, calculation logic, or the AMI vendor, each with a different owner and authority; cannot be scoped from current evidence alone.
U-LOCUS.resolution_path: Query the DA-RULES billing-config change log and obtain DA-MDMS AMI read events for a sample of disputed ACTUAL-read bills.
U-LOCUS.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostics using billing-db, route-log and billing-config only; do not scope any automated bill correction until the locus is confirmed.
U-LOCUS.resolution: Billing import validation rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling), deployed 2026-08-01, is identified as the billing-import-validation locus coincident with the dispute-surge onset and consistent with the AMI-read rejection pattern in E-12; the specific defect mechanism (possible unit mismatch) still needs confirmation.

U-MDMS-ACCESS.question: When will vendor-provisioned MDMS export access be available so AMI read events for disputed bills can be examined?
U-MDMS-ACCESS.decision_impact: Without AMI read events, the AMI-read-failure candidate mechanism cannot be confirmed or excluded, leaving a gap in the diagnosis.
U-MDMS-ACCESS.resolution_path: ORG-AMI vendor provisions MDMS export access per DA-MDMS acquisition note; retry mdms-export once access is granted (current tool_health DEGRADED, recent HOLD on ACCESS_PENDING).
U-MDMS-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI-read-failure as an open, untested candidate; proceed with available billing-db/route-log/billing-config evidence in the meantime.
U-MDMS-ACCESS.resolution: MDMS export access is now confirmed provisioned and operational: this AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE mdms-export tool record (E-12) successfully retrieved AMI read events, corroborating the earlier stakeholder claim (E-11/CL-04).

U-INTAKE-SHIFT.question: Did CRM ticket intake, categorization, or SLA-tracking configuration change around August 2026 in a way that inflates the apparent dispute count independent of actual bill errors?
U-INTAKE-SHIFT.decision_impact: If intake methodology shifted, part of the reported volume doubling (E-03) may be an artifact, changing the true magnitude of the problem and the volume-baseline target.
U-INTAKE-SHIFT.resolution_path: Audit CRM ticket intake/categorization/SLA-tracking configuration history (DA-TICKET) for changes around August 2026.
U-INTAKE-SHIFT.safe_placeholder: Treat the full E-03 volume trend as reflecting real disputes for monitoring/success-criteria purposes while this audit remains open.

U-FIELD-TIMING.question: How much of the route-completion shortfall and its disputed-bill impact overlaps in time and accounts with the dispute surge onset in August, given the reported staffing shortage dates to July?
U-FIELD-TIMING.decision_impact: Determines whether field-dispatch remediation is warranted now or should wait until a confirmed billing-side fix is scoped, affecting whether K-DISPATCH actions are needed.
U-FIELD-TIMING.resolution_path: Cross-tabulate route-log completion by month against CRM dispute timing and billing-db estimate-substitution flags.
U-FIELD-TIMING.safe_placeholder: Do not propose any push_route_update until the account-level overlap is quantified.

U-ACTUAL-LOCUS.question: What causes the majority 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of total, E-02)? H-ACTUAL-READ-CALC-ERROR remains an open candidate not yet tested beyond the ESTIMATED-subset AMI investigation (E-12).
U-ACTUAL-LOCUS.decision_impact: Determines whether any corrective scope beyond the confirmed BV-17/ESTIMATED mechanism is needed for the majority of disputed bills; affects release completeness.
U-ACTUAL-LOCUS.resolution_path: Query billing-db for ACTUAL-read disputed bills' calculation/tariff/import details and cross-check mdms-export read events to test H-ACTUAL-READ-CALC-ERROR.
U-ACTUAL-LOCUS.safe_placeholder: Report only the confirmed ESTIMATED-subset BV-17 finding as diagnosed; do not scope or claim any fix for ACTUAL-read bills until this locus is identified.

U-UNIT-SCALING-CONFIRM.question: Is the unit mismatch between v4.2 register output and BV-17's unscaled comparison the exact operative defect, as opposed to e.g. threshold miscalibration, for the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION reads?
U-UNIT-SCALING-CONFIRM.decision_impact: Determines the exact fix needed in BV-17 (unit scaling vs threshold recalibration vs other logic change) before any rule-change remedy can be designed.
U-UNIT-SCALING-CONFIRM.resolution_path: Trace a sample of the 1184 rejected reads' raw register values through BV-17's comparison logic against mdms-export and billing-config records.
U-UNIT-SCALING-CONFIRM.safe_placeholder: Treat the unit-scaling mismatch (E-13, E-14) as the leading diagnostic hypothesis only; do not scope or recommend a BV-17 rule-threshold change until directly confirmed.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the nightly MDMS-to-billing handoff (H-MDMS-BILL) delivering AMI register reads with confirmed delivery_status and semantic_validity, or could handoff-level issues confound the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern already attributed to BV-17/firmware (E-12-E-14)?
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If the handoff itself is unreliable, the BV-17/unit-scaling mechanism finding could be confounded by upstream data-quality issues, affecting confidence in the ESTIMATED-mechanism and ACTUAL-locus diagnostic criteria.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Check H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity fields against mdms-export records for the relevant period, alongside the DA-RULES/DA-BILL diagnostics already scoped.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Rely on the already-confirmed E-12/E-13/E-14 evidence as the current best mechanism explanation; flag any future handoff-validity finding as a potential confound rather than blocking release of the diagnostic finding.

A-OVERLAP.statement: The 9200 manual-read accounts affected by low route completion (E-01) are assumed to be a subset of, not identical to, the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-02); the exact overlap is not established by the cited evidence.

A-RULES-UNCHANGED-UNVERIFIED.statement: Absence of a logged tariff change (E-04) is assumed not to also mean billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) are unchanged; that log has not yet been queried as evidence.

A-TICKET-INTAKE-STABLE.statement: CRM ticket intake/categorization methodology is assumed unchanged across Jun-Sep 2026, so the volume trend in E-03 is assumed to measure real disputes rather than a logging-process artifact.

A-UNIT-SCALING-MECHANISM.statement: The unit mismatch between firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register output and BV-17's unscaled raw-register comparison is assumed to be the proximate rejection mechanism, based on correlated timing and plausibility (E-13, E-14) rather than a direct trace of rejected reads' register values.

key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS): build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix wrong bills. For the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3025, E-02), evidence shows 1184 (95%) were valid AMI reads rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on billing import (E-12), traced to validation rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13) combined with a firmware v4.2 register-unit mismatch (0.1 m3 vs m3, E-14); hypotheses H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE and H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE are CONFIRMED on this basis.
The mechanism behind the majority 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of total, E-02) remains unestablished (unknown U-ACTUAL-LOCUS, deferred as VOB-U-ACTUAL-LOCUS, status OPEN).

proposal.summary: The original request (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix wrong bills; evidence showed response times already meet SLA (E-05) and automated bill writes are barred by constraint K-BILLWRITE, so that framing was not carried forward. The problem was instead defined around a doubling of dispute tickets from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03). An earlier version of the problem (PD-1@v1), which blamed field manual-read shortfalls, was invalidated once evidence E-12 showed the 1240 "ESTIMATED" disputed bills (41% of 3025, E-02) were almost entirely AMI-channel reads rejected on billing import, not missing field reads. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) confirms that mechanism: billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), combined with firmware v4.2's register-unit mismatch (E-14), caused 1184 of those 1240 reads to be rejected as high-consumption and substituted with estimates. The cause of the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785, 59%) was not established and remains an open verification obligation (VOB-U-ACTUAL-LOCUS). The DEFINE Gate reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the recorded release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no hold items), releasing only a limited scope: an audit of CRM ticket-intake methodology (synthesizing E-03), with no automated bill-write capability included. Several diagnostic questions (unit-scaling confirmation, ACTUAL-read locus, MDMS handoff validity) remain open and are documented as known limitations, and the one structural fix identified for BV-17 is flagged as infeasible within contest time due to lack of a billing-config write tool, limiting this release to a diagnosis-and-recommendation outcome rather than a full fix.
